angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 1,182,690 km at 193.40 pc = 0.08 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 5.1705 +/- 0.0142 mas (same row, RUWE 0.89): 193.40 pc, no zero-point correction
radiusSource: Radius 1.7 +/- 0.02 solar radii from Battley et al. 2026, the stellar radius of the default parameter set of TOI-6564 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2026MNRAS.549g1053B/abstract): 1,182,690 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 1.18 +/- 0.16 solar masses from Battley et al. 2026, the stellar mass of the default parameter set of TOI-6564 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2026MNRAS.549g1053B/abstract); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 5943 +/- 64 K from Battley et al. 2026, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of TOI-6564 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2026MNRAS.549g1053B/abstract). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Battley et al. 2026, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of TOI-6564 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2026MNRAS.549g1053B/abstract)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/toi-6564.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 4.049, rounded to two decimals
